description: An uneven lump of leathery flesh.  Why does it wobble like that?  Is it even alive?
A small, flat disc that seems to be made out of bronze or brass.  It has several intricate engravings etched into the surface.
A lopsided lump of pale, translucent crystal.  Might be quartz, but as far as you're aware quartz doesn't look like a window into a cloudy space considerably bigger than itself.

Several feet of linen cord, haphazardly tied into a rat's nest of impossible structure.  Trying to follow either end of it seems to require more than three dimensions to make something this tangled.  This probably isn't what they meant by string theory.
A shiny, perfectly round crystal ball.  It has a faint sea-green tint to it, but seems extremely hard to so much as chip.
A perfectly smooth-faced cube made out of a dull gray metal.  It seems notably dense, the sort of cube that could cure your mortality.
A hollow shell of dark ceramic, vaguely resembling an animal-like silhouette with numerous holes in it.  Part of it looks like it was meant to be either a handle or an ornate crest.
//: Todo: if we ever mainline clay oil lamps from MST Extra, change the looks_like accordingly.

description: A short baton made of a hard ivory, textured with a spiral pattern as though carved from a narwhal's tusk.  It's far too perfectly straight and geometrically consistent to be naturally-grown.
A short, ornate golden spike.  It comes to an impossibly thin point, the surface faintly marked with silvery lines that form an alluring fractal pattern, infinitely smaller as it nears the tip.
A finely-made necklace made of polished stone beads.  The only odd thing is they don't have any holes in them nor any string, and yet they stay together just fine.
A small ring of carved stone resembling a snake or worm.  It's coiled towards itself like an ouroboros, except you can't find either end of it, it just keeps spiraling around.

What seems to be a beautiful cloth scarf with a scintillating weave of ever-changing patterns.  It doesn't seem very warm however, and it vaguely feels like the individual threads are squirming at your touch.

A single decorative arm guard made of metal, covering most of the forearm.  Every surface has been polished to a mirror finish.  You're fairly certain that's not your reflection distorted on its curved surface, however.
